name: Adaptive capability

subjectOf.text: Rulemaking with dynamic elements increases the adaptive capabilities of financial regulation through the increasing use of institution specific information, including information on how financial institutions and their decision makers actually act and are expected to react to unforeseen contingencies.
subjectOf.abstract: Rulemaking with dynamic elements increases the adaptive capabilities of financial regulation through the increasing use of institution specific information.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Dynamic Regulation of the Financial Services Industry (2013). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2273857
scope_conditions: institution specific information is actually generated and available

subjectOf.text: The social and mental properties of decision makers in financial institutions, combined with the incentive structure of the respective institutional setup, determine a financial institution's adaptive capability.
subjectOf.abstract: Social and mental properties of decision makers in financial institutions together with the incentive structure in the respective institutional setups can help determine a financial institution's adaptive capability.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Dynamic Regulation of the Financial Services Industry (2013). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2273857

subjectOf.text: A mixture of mandatory rules, market solutions, and private ordering would increase the adaptive capabilities of rulemaking, curtail the effects of the collective action problem of rulemaking, and dampen regulatory cycles.
subjectOf.abstract: A mixture of mandatory rules, market solutions, and private ordering could help increase the adaptive capabilities of rulemaking, curtail the effects of the collective action problem of rulemaking, and dampen regulatory cycles.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Dynamic Regulation of the Financial Services Industry (2013). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2273857
scope_conditions: mixed regime combining mandatory and private mechanisms
